gi.master.emitter.spotlight-left.note: Left chrome GI spotlight, independently visible in the stock NIB Pro photo and owner GI inventory. Source pixel is the housing-head projection, not the lower spotlight mounting post or an under-plastic sling socket; no visible filament is claimed.

gi.master.emitter.spotlight-right.note: Right chrome GI spotlight housing-head projection. This is separate from switched Q27 Magneto spotlight and from the two hidden right-sling wedge bulbs.

flasher.left-side.emitter.upper.note: Left upper dome: actual dark circular housing, corroborated by a second independently read Pro drawing; no render sprite supplies this position.

flasher.left-side.emitter.lower.note: Left lower dome: own actual housing center, with a second Pro drawing read and one emitter per dome.

flasher.right-side.emitter.upper.note: Right upper dome: corrected from the reader's left-edge point to the actual circular housing center. Cross-drawing residual records scan/fit uncertainty.

flasher.right-side.emitter.lower.note: Right lower dome: actual housing center, separately measured from its companion; second Pro drawing corroborates it.

device.wolverine-flasher.emitter.note: Factory 21 identifies the separate #89 Wolverine insert flasher. Projected onto its own round bulb/assembly end, not the remote 21 balloon or matrix 31 label; a second Pro drawing corroborates the coarse plan position.

device.pop-bumper-flasher.emitter.note: Factory 25 names the #89 flasher below the Gambit/pop area. Projected onto the visible round bulb assembly under that balloon; matrix 16 is its separate controlled insert lamp.

lamp.left-eject-top-59.emitter.note: One #555 scoop-top lamp: the 59 label covers its own lamp assembly. This is a disclosed plan projection through that physical part, rounded to scan precision; it is not a filament measurement or f59b reflection.

reassessment.reason: Actual Pro disassembly and first-hand lock-entry left/right description positively identify the paired large-collar flasher assemblies, distinct from horizontal 31 and a threaded post. Three hardware landmarks resolve the association that alignment alone could not. Own-assembly projections are now accepted; the initial rejection is preserved below as history.

q22-left.reason: A real concentric assembly is visible below the 22 balloon. Its alignment does not prove that it is the flasher socket, its base rather than bulb, or another fitting. Generic socket profile and lack of a GI leader do not establish positive Q22 circuit identity. Excluded from canonical placements after independent reassessment.

q22-right.reason: Same unresolved body/socket-base association as left. The two upper 22 balloons cover geometry and cannot themselves be substituted as emitter centers. Exact Pro quantityX 2 remains proven independently.

gi.master.reason: Partial census of 35 actual Pro body/projection records. B01, H02, H04 are accepted from positive white-GI counterpart endpoints and actual Pro mounted-body continuity; plain ring appearance alone did not decide them. B02 and UL2 remain unclassified. Whole quantity cannot be inferred from owner totals or absence of another endpoint; remaining observed geometry also prevents promotion.

q31_candidate.reason: Horizontal body immediately below 31 box has a base, cylindrical section and rounded dark end. It resembles the lifted figure fixture but may be adjacent gate/lock hardware; proximity and shape do not positively assign it to 31. The actual figure lamp is fitted, but this candidate must not become a socket coordinate until its installed mounting correspondence is proven. Local spotlight-photo controls do not bracket the raised figure head.

manufacturer_alternative.decision: candidate_only: visible skirt is raised, outside control hull and does not identify the actual installed socket mount. A full-frame control fit alone does not resolve that physical projection.

rejected_trough_contact_projection.corner_roles: Exit/right guideplate end, entrance/right end, entrance/left end, exit/left end. Four observed physical top-plane corners rectify to(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1); no nominal ball spacing is assumed.
rejected_trough_contact_projection.target_roles: Historical Pro guideplate axis used by the rejected calculation. It does not turn photographed wiring hardware into switch geometry.
rejected_trough_contact_projection.limits: Withdrawn after source inspection: the first two pixels are nylon cable-tie heads and the third is a white harness clip/connector. They are not actuator tips. Former coordinates are rejected history only, with no accepted spatial placements. The cutaway still establishes microswitch order 18/19/20 and vertically stacked exit optos 21/22; individual contact geometry remains unproved.

excerpt.image_derivation: Native 3000 x 2000 actual Pro photo SHA-256 3b772d7e2544f4f3277c148f8174aecb7345af64b5fe0358add5dae60dfe8088; native crop (1050, 1060, 1330, 1320), 280x260, no resize or assumed DPI. Pillow 12.3.0, grayscale WebP quality 80 method 6, tools/xmen_pro_drawing_geometry.py. Tight own-fixture reading aid; complete control overlay stays external.

flasher.magneto-spotlight.emitter.scope: One bounded local physical assembly measurement, not a whole-playfield drawing/callout validation. Ten independently reconciled insert centers surround the target; convex-hull containment and leave-one-out 0.07 limit are mandatory. Existing whole-page controls/span rules are unchanged.
flasher.magneto-spotlight.emitter.note: Actual Pro Q27 chrome spotlight at the front-left of Magneto: observed image projection of its raised head/stem joint, not a playfield-plane mounting point. Ten surrounding insert controls provide a reproducible local 2D fit, but the joint is above that plane and its height/parallax are unmeasured. Low leave-one-out error and hull containment validate image calibration only. The coordinate remains observed with coplanarity unproved; neither the remote 27 box nor a sprite supplies a physical socket center. This spotlight is separate from both GI spots above the slings.

pro-factory-rear.locator: Michael Minn factory tour, 2012-08-26, 14-36-54 photograph; actual back side of Pro rear board, native crop (550, 1310, 1670, 1830)

controls.point: rear-view upper-left board end = player right; own Pro p20 frame(1375,330) through independent fit
rear-view upper-right board end = player left; own Pro p20 frame(170,330) through independent fit

pro-factory-rear.axis_basis: Top board edge joins (38,94) to (1110,8); visible left edge joins (38,94) to (90,475). These are observed affine axes, not a four-corner perspective solution. Lower right corner is concealed. No emitter spacing was assumed.
pro-factory-rear.plane_basis: Vertical rear-board emitters project to the physical rear boundary, y=0. This is a disclosed own-panel plan projection; photo height is never normalized as playfield y. The Pro CAD top profile independently locates this rear-edge assembly.
pro-factory-rear.limitations: Two endpoint controls do not meet the four-control elevation validation requirement. All twelve points remain observed. Pro photo itself establishes six forward GI bulbs and six hanging #89 flashers, including the close center pair. LE assembly sheet is a corroborating fitting/topology key only; no LE coordinate or Pro part-number identity is assumed.
